senses.gloss:
child-marriage
------------------------------------------
Child-मर्रिअगे has often been a subject of criticism against the Hindu society. But छिल्द्-मर्रिअगे was not a peculiar phenomenon of the Hindu society alone. It existed even in England during the middle of the 16th century.
During the times of the ऋग्वेद, it was unheard of. Till A.D. 200, मर्रिअगे of girls just before or after puberty was the rule. Girls could be married even up to or after three years, after puberty. If the parents did not get them married even then, the grown-up girls had the freedom to choose their husbands (vide मनुस्मृति 9.89-90).
However, the situation changed after A. D. 200 and child-marriages became more a rule than an exception. Some scholars opine that the rise of the institution of Buddhist nuns by about this period and the laxity of morals among the nuns forced the Hindu society to adopt छिल्द्-मर्रिअगे as a counter measure. The age of girls for मर्रिअगे was usually 6 to 8 years, an equivalent of the age of the boys for उपनयन (the ceremony of investiture with the sacred thread).
These child-marriages were however mere sacraments of betrothal and the child couple continued to live with their parents. Consummation took place only after puberty.
During those days, joint family system was very much in vogue. The child couples were received into the big family with love and affection. Hence there were practically no problems of psychological adjustment on either side.
It cannot of course be denied that things were often taken to ridiculous lengths, resulting sometimes in the cruel problem of child widows.
It will be of interest to note here that all the rules of the धर्मशास्त्रस् regarding छिल्द्-मर्रिअगे were only for the ब्राह्मणस् and did not affect the other sections of the Hindu society.
See also VIVĀHA.
